source_text: μᾶλλον ὑπ' αὐτῇ, καὶ δι' αὐτὴν καὶ ὑπὸ πόδας αὐτῆς ὡς ποιήματα; προκατήρξατο γὰρ εὐδοκήσας ὁ πατήρ, ἐδημιούργησεν δὲ ὁ μονογενὴς υἱός, ἡγίασεν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τῷ ἁγιασμῷ αὐτοῦ ἐτελείωσεν, ἐφώτισεν, ἐδυνάμωσεν, ἐζωοδότησεν· 1.7 ἐν πᾶσιν καὶ ἐν ἑκάστῳ ὅλον ὑπάρχον, καὶ ὑπὸ ὅλων ὅλον μετεχόμενον καὶ χωρούμενον δι' ἀγαθότητα· καὶ μὴ μεριζόμενον, μήτε μετερχόμενον ἢ μεταβαλλόμενον· ἀλλ' ἀεὶ πᾶσιν ἐπιπνέον ὁμοίως, καὶ οὐκ ἐν μέρει, καὶ φυλάττον τὴν οἰκείαν ἄχραντον ἀπὸ τῶν σωμάτων καθαρότητα, πάντα τε θείως καταλάμπον καὶ πανταχοῦ πληθύον ἁγιασμόν, ἀγάπην, εἰρήνην, σοφίαν. χαράν, ἀσφάλειαν καὶ πᾶν ἀγαθόν, ἅτε ἐκ τῆς πατρικῆς ἐνυποστάτως ἔκλαμψαν πηγῆς· 1.8 δι' οὗ καὶ δι' ὃ ἡμῖν πλησιάζει ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατήρ, μεθ' οὗ καὶ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἐστιν καὶ παρ' ἡμῖν μένει· δυναμένης μὲν ἑκάστης θείας ὑποστάσεως ἀπροσδεῶς πάντα ποιῆσαι τελείως, ἵνα δὲ δειχθῇ τὸ συμπρακτικὸν καὶ ἀπαράλλακτον τῆς τε οὐσίας αὐτῶν τῆς τε προσκυνήσεως καὶ δόξης καὶ εὐχαριστίας τῆς ὀφειλούσης παρ' ἡμῶν γίνεσθαι, διὰ τοῦτο κοινῇ παρὰ τῆς ἁγίας τριάδος τῆς κτίσεως πληρωθείσης. 1.9 παριστῶν γοῦν τὸ τριαδικῶς διακεκοσμῆσθαι τὴν κτίσιν ψάλλει· «τῷ λόγῳ κυρίου οἱ οὐρανοὶ ἐστερεώθησαν, καὶ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ πᾶσαι αἱ δυνάμεις αὐτῶν.» εἶπεν γὰρ «κύριον» μὲν τὸν θεὸν πατέρα, «λόγον» δὲ τὸν μονογενῆ υἱόν, δι' οὗ καὶ 42 παρ' οὗ ἐκτίσθησαν, «πνεῦμα» δὲ τὸ ἐνυπόστατον ἅγιον πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ, παρ' οὗ ἁγιασθέντες ἐνεδυναμώθησαν. 1.10 αὐτὸ γάρ ἐστιν τὸ θεϊκὸν ὄνομα, τὸ παντοκρατορικὸν καὶ ὑπερέχον ἀξίωμα, τὸ σὺν πατρὶ καὶ υἱῷ μνημονευόμενον καὶ συνδοξαζόμενον· τὸ ἁγιαστικὸν καὶ ζωοποιὸν καὶ φωτὸς οὐρανίου μεταδοτικόν· τὸ φρουρητικὸν ἑκάστων τῆς ἐν ταυτότητι διαμονῆς· τὸ προφήταις καὶ ἀποστόλοις ἐνηχῆσαν, καὶ μάρτυρας ἀντιστῆναι τυραννικῇ ὠμότητι ἐνισχύσαν· τὸ ἀνακαινίζον καὶ ἐλευθεροῦν ὡς κύριος, καὶ υἱοὺς θεοῦ ἡμᾶς ποιοῦν ὡς πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας· τὸ ἀπελαῦνον τῷ φωτίσματι δαιμόνων στίφη, καὶ τὸν ἀντικείμενον καταισχύνον· τὸ ἀναπετάζον ἡμῖν τὰς οὐρανῶν πύλας, καὶ ἄγον ἐπὶ τὴν εἴσοδον τῆς σωτηρίας, καὶ τῆς ἀγγέλων πολιτείας καὶ ὑμνῳδίας ἐργαζόμενον κοινωνούς· 1.11 τὸ γινόμενον ἡμῖν τρίβος ἀποφέρουσα πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπουράνιον θεὸν καὶ πατέρα· ἡ αὐτεξούσιος καὶ ὑπερβάλλουσα γαληνοτάτη ἐπιφάνεια· ἡ γόνιμος καὶ ἄπειρος καὶ σωστικὴ δύναμις· ἡ ἀμεγέθης καὶ ἀσύγκριτος καὶ σεπτὴ ὑπόστασις· ἡ ἄχραντος καὶ ἔγκριτος καὶ πάναγνος δόξα· ἡ θεία χάρις ἡ τὰ λείποντα ἀναπληροῦσα καὶ τὰ ἀσθενῆ ἰωμένη· ἡ ἄρρητος καὶ ἀίδιος ἀγαθότης· ἡ πηγὴ τῶν ἀνεκλείπτων χαρισμάτων καὶ παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ νοῦ πρόοδος· ἡ μελλόντων καὶ ἀγνώστων ἀληθὴς φανέρωσις· 1.12 ἡ σωτήριος σφραγὶς καὶ τὸ θεῖον χρῖσμα, ὁ ἀρραβὼν τῶν ἀιδίων ἀγαθῶν, παρ' οὗ πᾶσα κτίσις, ὁρατὴ καὶ ἀόρατος, λογικὴ καὶ μὴ λογική, ἐνδυναμοῦται· παρ' οὗ ἡμῖν ἡ θεία ἀναγέννησις καὶ τῶν ἀνομιῶν ἡ ἄφεσις καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡ ἐπικάλυψις καὶ ἡ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν οἰκείωσις· στέφανός τε δικαίοις καὶ ἀγαθῶν ἀπόληψις· οὐράνιόν τε ἐνδιαίτημα καὶ ζωὴ ἀτηλεύτητος καὶ βασιλείας θεοῦ κληρονομία αἰώνιος· 1.13 οὗτινος τῆς κοινωνίας διὰ τῆς παλιγγεννεσίας ὁ μετέχων τυγχάνει τῶν μνημονευθέντων ἀγαθῶν καὶ πρὸς τὰς καθολικὰς ἐπιστολὰς θείας ἐστὶ κοινωνὸς φύσεως. ὁ γὰρ ἀφθάρτου καὶ ἀιδίου φωτίσματος μετειληφὼς ἀγήρως κατὰ τὸ νοητὸν μένει ἐν νεότητι καὶ ἠπιότητι, καὶ ἐξομοιοῦται τῷ μόνῳ ἔχοντι ἀθανασίαν καὶ φῶς οἰκοῦντι ἀπρόσιτον. 1.14 οἱ γὰρ τῆς ἀρχαίας καὶ νέας διαθήκης ἱερομάνται τῆς ἀνωτάτω μιᾶς θείας θύσεως εἶναι τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἐπίστανται. αὐτίκα γοῦν μαρτυροῦσιν· 2.ν Περὶ τοῦ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα εἶναι τοῦ θεοῦ· καὶ περὶ αἱρετικῆς ἀντιθέσεως 2.1 Πρῶτον μέν, ὅτι πνεῦμά ἐστι τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰ καὶ μὴ μετ'
pass_a_gloss: [... but all things are] rather under it, and on account of it, and under its feet as things made? For the Father, having been well pleased, began first, and the only-begotten Son crafted, and the Spirit of God sanctified, and by his sanctification perfected, enlightened, empowered, gave life; 1.7 being whole in all and in each one, and shared in and received whole by all wholly, on account of goodness; and not being divided, nor moving from place to place or being changed; but always breathing upon all alike, and not in part, and guarding its own purity undefiled by bodies, and divinely shining on all things and everywhere multiplying sanctification, love, peace, wisdom, joy, security and every good, as having shone forth with its own subsistence from the paternal fountain; 1.8 through whom and on account of whom the God and Father draws near to us, with whom he both is in the heavens and stays with us; each divine hypostasis being able, without need of anything, to make all things perfectly, but so that there be shown the working-together and the unvarying [sameness] both of their essence and of the worship and glory and thanksgiving that ought to come from us, for this reason the creation having been brought to fullness in common by the holy Trinity. 1.9 Presenting, then, the creation's having been set in order in the manner of the Trinity, he sings: 'by the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the spirit of his mouth all their powers'. For he called God the Father 'Lord', and the only-begotten Son 'word', through whom and by whom they were created, and 'spirit' the subsisting Holy Spirit of God, by whom, having been sanctified, they were empowered. 1.10 For it is the divine name, the almighty and surpassing dignity, the one remembered and glorified together with Father and Son; the sanctifying and life-making one and imparter of heavenly light; the guardian of each thing's continuance in sameness; the one that sounded in prophets and apostles, and strengthened martyrs to stand against tyrannical cruelty; the one renewing and freeing as Lord, and making us sons of God as spirit of adoption; the one driving off by its illumination throngs of demons, and putting the adversary to shame; the one throwing open for us the gates of the heavens, and leading to the entrance of salvation, and making [us] sharers of the citizenship and hymn-singing of angels; 1.11 the one becoming for us a path carrying [us] toward the heavenly God and Father himself; the self-determining and surpassing, most serene manifestation; the fruitful and boundless and saving power; the sizeless and incomparable and venerable hypostasis; the undefiled and choice and all-pure glory; the divine grace that fills up the things lacking and heals the weak things; the unspeakable and everlasting goodness; the fountain of the unfailing gifts and advance of every good mind; the true disclosure of things to come and unknown; 1.12 the saving seal and the divine anointing, the pledge of the everlasting goods, by whom all creation, seen and unseen, rational and not rational, is empowered; by whom [there is] for us the divine rebirth and the release of the lawless deeds and the covering of the sins and the being made kin toward God; and a crown for the righteous and a receiving of good things; and a heavenly dwelling and unending life and everlasting inheritance of the kingdom of God; 1.13 whose fellowship the one sharing in it through the rebirth obtains the goods mentioned, and according to the catholic epistles is a sharer of divine nature. For the one who has received the incorruptible and everlasting illumination remains ageless as to the intelligible, in youth and gentleness, and is made like the one alone having immortality and dwelling in unapproachable light. 1.14 For the sacred seers of the old and new covenant know the Holy Spirit to be of the highest one divine nature (the copy-text reads 'sacrifice'). For instance, then, they testify: 2.ν [Chapter title:] On the Holy Spirit's being of God; and on a heretical objection. 2.1 First, that he is Spirit of God and from God, even if not after [...]
pass_b_english: … rather beneath it, and for its sake, and under its feet as its works? For the Father, in his good pleasure, made the first beginning; the only-begotten Son fashioned; and the Spirit of God sanctified, and by his sanctification perfected, enlightened, strengthened and gave life.

He is whole in all and whole in each; all share in him and receive him whole, because of his goodness. He is not divided, he does not pass from place to place, he does not change. He breathes on all things always and alike, not in part, and keeps his own purity unstained by bodies. He shines divinely on all things and everywhere multiplies sanctification, love, peace, wisdom, joy, security and every good, since he has shone forth, subsisting in his own right, from the Father’s fountain.

Through him and because of him the God and Father draws near to us; with him the Father both is in the heavens and abides with us. Each divine hypostasis could, needing nothing further, have made all things perfectly. But the creation was brought to fullness in common by the Holy Trinity for this reason: to show that they work together, and that nothing varies between them, neither their essence nor the worship, glory and thanksgiving that we owe.

So, to present the creation as set in order by the Trinity, he sings: “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the spirit of his mouth all their powers” (Psalm 33:6). For he called God the Father “Lord”; the only-begotten Son “word”, through whom and by whom they were created; and “spirit” the Holy Spirit of God, who subsists in his own right, by whom they were sanctified and strengthened.

For he is the divine name, the almighty and surpassing dignity, the one named and glorified together with Father and Son; the one who sanctifies, gives life and imparts heavenly light; the one who keeps each thing abiding in its identity; the one who sounded within prophets and apostles and strengthened martyrs to stand against the cruelty of tyrants; the one who renews and sets free as Lord, and makes us sons of God as the Spirit of adoption (Romans 8:15); the one who by his illumination drives off the hosts of demons and puts the adversary to shame; the one who throws open to us the gates of heaven, leads us to the entrance of salvation, and makes us sharers in the angels’ way of life and in their hymns.

He becomes for us the path that carries us to the heavenly God and Father himself. He is the sovereign, surpassing and most serene manifestation; the fruitful, boundless and saving power; the hypostasis beyond all magnitude, beyond compare and worthy of reverence; the undefiled, chosen and all-pure glory; the divine grace that fills up what is lacking and heals what is weak; the unspeakable and everlasting goodness; the fountain of unfailing gifts and the advance of every good mind; the true disclosure of things to come and things unknown.

He is the saving seal and the divine anointing, the pledge of everlasting good things, by whom all creation, visible and invisible, rational and irrational, is strengthened. From him we have the divine rebirth, the forgiveness of lawless deeds and the covering of sins (Psalm 32:1), and kinship with God; from him come a crown for the righteous and the receiving of good things, a dwelling in heaven, life without end, and the everlasting inheritance of the kingdom of God.

Whoever shares in his fellowship through rebirth obtains the good things just named and, as the catholic epistles say, becomes a sharer in the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4). For one who has received the incorruptible and everlasting illumination stays ageless in mind, in youthfulness and gentleness, and is made like him who alone has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16).
For the sacred seers of the old and the new covenant know that the Holy Spirit belongs to the one supreme divine nature. Here, for instance, is their witness.
That the Holy Spirit is of God; and on a heretical objection.

choices.issue: Old draft garbled, broken and labelled
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed edition numbers 1.11, 1.12, 1.13, 1.14, '2.N' and 2.1 in the reading text and ran the chapter title into the prose; broke 1.10 off at 'renews...' and restarted 'And they free us'; called the Trinity 'her' and read δι' αὐτήν as 'by her'; read τρίβος (path) as 'tribulation', ἄπειρος (boundless) as 'inexperienced', ἔγκριτος (choice) as 'stable', σεπτή (venerable) as 'pure', ἐνδιαίτημα (dwelling) as 'sustenance', ἠπιότητι (gentleness) as 'freshness', 'toward the catholic epistles' for 'according to'; mangled the 1.8 purpose clause ('since creation is fulfilled'); and made 1.14 say 'the priests … are the Holy Spirit of the one supreme divine sacrifice'. Psalm 33:6 kept (LXX 32:6); Romans 8:15, Psalm 32:1, 2 Peter 1:4 and 1 Timothy 6:16 added.

choices.why: The section opens mid-question; the previous section ends 'but all things'. αὐτῇ is the Trinity (feminine τριάς), so 'it', not 'her'. Only the words this section holds are translated, with a leading ellipsis.
διά with the accusative gives the cause or end, not the agent; the old 'by her' read it as a genitive.

choices.english: shone forth, subsisting in his own right / who subsists in his own right
choices.why: Didymus stresses that the Spirit is a hypostasis, not an energy; 'hypostatic' is jargon in the reading text.
Each Person could act without need of another; the old 'without hindrance' changed the sense.

choices.term: τὸ συμπρακτικὸν καὶ ἀπαράλλακτον τῆς τε οὐσίας … τῆς τε προσκυνήσεως
choices.english: that they work together, and that nothing varies between them, neither their essence nor the worship …
choices.why: Neuter adjectives used as nouns, broken into two clauses; the genitives name what is unvarying.

choices.english: set in order by the Trinity
choices.why: The adverb means 'in the manner of the Trinity'; the following gloss names Father, Son and Spirit as the agents, so 'by the Trinity' keeps the sense in plain English.
Not 'breath': Didymus' argument turns on the word πνεῦμα naming the Holy Spirit.

choices.english: the advance of every good mind
choices.why: πρόοδος set beside πηγή could also mean 'going forth'; 'advance' (progress) fits a list of the Spirit's gifts to believers and adds no doctrine of procession.
The agelessness is of the intelligible, inner life, not the body.
The copy-text's θύσεως (sacrifice) makes no sense with 'the one supreme divine'; read as a slip for φύσεως (nature), a one-letter error. Recorded under problems.

choices.english: Here, for instance, is their witness.
choices.why: αὐτίκα in argument introduces an example; the testimonies follow the chapter title.

choices.term: 2.ν Περὶ τοῦ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα εἶναι τοῦ θεοῦ
choices.english: That the Holy Spirit is of God; and on a heretical objection.
choices.why: Chapter title set as its own short paragraph.
The section ends on the elided preposition; the next section begins with its object αὐτόν (accusative, so 'after', not 'with'). The sentence is finished there, not here.
'42' is a printed page number in the copy-text; skipped.
